note: The iteration loop: prototype, test it rigorously, and analyze what failed to feed the next build.
Fast hardware iteration: build prototypes, choose tooling by rate, and keep the design cheap to make.
Two advanced fabrication methods that turn a design into a physical part.
Qualifying a made part: produce it, run the test campaign, and establish the qualification basis.
Manufacturing readiness: a producible design, the right tooling, and the chosen fabrication process.
Proving and controlling the configuration: qualify it, analyze failures, and manage changes with traceability.
Weight control meets design trades: mass budgets drive material, layup, and manufacturability decisions.
Program control: configuration and effectivity, qualification status, and mass tracking all follow the same baseline.
